BV","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"<jats:p>We study the construction of statistically valid prediction sets for gradient-boosted regression models when the test covariate distribution P test X differs from the calibration distribution P cal X-a setting known as covariate shift. Standard split conformal prediction achieves finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability, but this guarantee collapses arbitrarily when the covariate distribution shifts. We develop a unified framework combining importance-weighted conformal scores with novel variance-reduction techniques via self-normalised importance weights. Our central contribution is a sharp impossibility theorem characterising regimes where conditional coverage is fundamentally unattainable (Theorem 3.2), paired with adaptive prediction sets (APS) that achieve near-optimal conditional coverage rates whenever the likelihood ratio is estimable at a sufficient rate (Theorem 4.3). We further introduce a covariate-adaptive bandwidth selection procedure for locally weighted conformal inference that is provably consistent under mild regularity conditions (Theorem 5.2). Experiments on twelve real-world tabular benchmarksincluding MIMIC-IV, FRED, and UCI repository datasets-demonstrate that our method maintains 90% marginal coverage with average interval width reductions of 23-41% over baseline weighted conformal methods, with robustness to moderate likelihood-ratio
